questions.prompt: Average volume is 120,000 contracts. Today 300,000 trade. What is the relative volume?

options.explanation: No: that is average ÷ today. Divide today by the average.

questions.prompt: Swing low 80.00, swing high 100.00. Where is the 61.8% retracement?

options.explanation: No: 61.8% is a share of the move, not a price.

questions.prompt: Downtrend; the last lower high is 1.3400. Price rallies to 1.3350 and turns down. Is the downtrend structure intact?

options.text: No: any rally ends a downtrend
options.explanation: No: rallies within a downtrend are normal. The question is whether one breaks the last lower high.
Right: 1.3350 is below 1.3400, so this is a pullback so far.
No: nothing broke. A reversal needs the structure to break first.

questions.prompt: Stock A falls from 80 to 76. Its index falls from 2,000 to 1,800. What is true?

options.text: A outperformed, so A went up
options.explanation: No: A fell 5%. It just fell less than the index.

options.text: The ratio fell because both prices fell
options.explanation: No: 76 ÷ 1,800 is higher than 80 ÷ 2,000, so the ratio rose.

options.text: A fell less, so the ratio rose

questions.prompt: You bought 100 shares at 25.50 with a stop at 24.00. The stock closes at 25.00 and opens at 23.50. Roughly what is the loss?

options.explanation: No: the open is below the stop, so the stop fills near 23.50, not 24.00.
No: 50 USD is only the extra loss from the gap: (24.00 − 23.50) × 100.

questions.prompt: Which pairs show a way these tools can mislead? Select all that apply.

options.text: Channel lines: redrawn after every candle
options.explanation: Right: lines that keep moving to fit price say nothing.

options.text: Volume: never, since it counts real trades
options.explanation: No: heavy-volume moves can fail, and forex tick volume is only a stand-in.
Right: with five levels close together, many turns land near one by chance.
